summary: A tactical, no-luck card-driven fighting game where each of the four heroes (Invisible Man, Sherlock & Watson, Dracula, Jekyll & Hyde) plays with a wildly different toolkit and win condition on a small point-to-point map. Matches are quick, tense duels decided by bluffing which card you'll play for attack, defense, or scheme value rather than by randomness.
praised: Deep asymmetry between heroes with genuinely distinct playstyles and win patterns
Fast setup and short playtime relative to the strategic depth
Sherlock & Watson's two-body mechanic and Invisible Man's stealth add fresh twists to the system
Rewards mastery and improves a lot with repeated plays against the same opponent
criticised: Steep learning curve for new players facing experienced ones due to hidden hero-specific tech
Some heroes (notably Invisible Man) are considered fiddly or swingy compared to others
Card draw variance can still occasionally overwhelm skill in a single short match
Small box means less content than some other Unmatched sets

interaction.kind: direct combat, positioning, and bluffing over card play

scoring.why: The game ends when one player reduces all opposing heroes' health to zero (or meets a hero-specific special condition), so combat efficiency alone decides the winner
